why5.question: Why cannot 16P #7 claim verified expiry and revocation?
why5.answer: Main currently has no merged CLOSURE_DEFERRAL and no real revocation docket; synthetic positive/negative self-tests cannot establish provider-end-to-end enforcement.

why5.question: Why add a real-clock integration probe?
why5.answer: The existing negative suite injects fake time. A GitHub-hosted job using actual wall-clock expiry and actual on-disk revocation events strengthens engine-level evidence without requiring Product changes.

why5.question: Why retain AUTHORITY_REQUIRED for protected lifecycle?
why5.answer: Temporary synthetic approval-shaped dockets are not Human-authorized merged exceptions. Only a correctly approved protected lifecycle can prove external host enforcement.

why5.question: Why use exactly two harness paths?
why5.answer: The new isolated clock runner is invoked from the existing 16P PR workflow. The other change recognizes already-authorized Sprint3 HOLD historical T008 evidence without inventing active execution authority.

why5.question: Why does this remain a Draft?
why5.answer: Exact source SHA/digest awaits separate Human approval; no authority to auto-merge, change Main, or treat fixture owner data as a real signature.

alternatives: Wait for current governance exception TTL (does not test CLOSURE_DEFERRAL).
Temporarily disable branch protection or bypass Human controls (prohibited).
Add bounded GitHub runner real-clock engine evidence; keep full provider E2E NOT_VERIFIED (chosen).

rollback: Remove this candidate-only 16P runner probe if authorized independent review identifies any false-green or side effect.
